glosses: To help keep from falling.

examples.text: Don’t move that beam! It supports the whole platform.

glosses: To back or favor a cause, party, etc., mentally or with concrete aid

examples.text: I support France in the World Cup.

glosses: To provide sustenance or maintenance for; to sustain in integrity or livelihood.

examples.text: Mars does not currently support human habitation.
A grain, which in England is generally given to horſes, but which in Scotland ſupports the people.

glosses: To help, particularly financially; to subsidize.

examples.text: I said I shouldn’t support anything that deceives people.
The government supports the arts in several ways.
The NIAID supports projects at universities and research organizations around the United States as well as a network of 21 NIAID labs across the country.

glosses: To provide evidence for; to lend credibility to.

examples.text: The testimony is not sufficient to support the charges.
The evidence will not support the statements or allegations.
to urge such arguments, as though they were sufficient to support and demonstrate a whole scheme of moral philosophy

glosses: To serve, as in a customer-oriented position; to give support to.

examples.text: The IT Department supports the research organization, but not the sales force.

glosses: To assist or be involved with, but not be responsible for.

examples.text: I support the administrative activities of the executive branch of the organization.
I don't make decisions, but I support those who do.

glosses: To answer questions and resolve problems regarding something sold.

examples.text: Sure they sell the product, but do they support it?

glosses: To be designed to provide capacity for; to work or be compatible with (a part, accessory, file type, program, algorithm, etc.).

examples.text: Early personal computers did not support voice-recognition hardware or software.

glosses: To endure without being overcome; bear; undergo; tolerate.

examples.text: This fierce demeanour and his insolence / The patience of a god could not support.
For a strong affection such moments are worth supporting, and they will end well; for your advocate is in your lover's heart and speaks her own language[…]

glosses: To play a lesser part in the same production with (a star performer).

examples.text: to support the character of King Lear
